name: Verify this estate yourself
description: A runnable, dependency-free verifier for the whole evidence chain. Free forever, no account, nothing to pay, and it trusts no Council of AI service.
principle: A body that asks others to show their evidence must let anyone check its own, without asking us. This door is that check, as a script rather than a promise.

run_it.requires: Node >= 18. No dependencies — Ed25519 comes from node:crypto.

what_it_checks: every signed card fetches, and its id equals sha256 of its own canonical body
each card body agrees with signed/card_index.json on id, signature and pubkey
the card signing key is the one published in the DID document on csoai.org
root.json's signature verifies against the key it names, using the preimage rule root.json publishes about itself
whether the root carries a timechain anchor — reported honestly either way

trust_model.note: The evidence and the keys come from different hosts, and the arithmetic runs on your machine. No Council of AI service is trusted at any step.

result_2026_09_05.indexed_urls_resolving: 664/664 across the doors and interop indexes

known_trap_for_reimplementers.problem: The per-card preimage_rule is a Python expression: json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True). Two of its behaviours do not reproduce in JavaScript.
known_trap_for_reimplementers.one: ensure_ascii=True escapes non-ASCII as \uXXXX; JSON.stringify emits it literally.
known_trap_for_reimplementers.two: Python renders a whole-number float as 1.0; JavaScript has a single number type and renders it as 1. Measured on this chain: 117 of 335 cards (34.9%) carry an accuracy that is a whole-number float.
known_trap_for_reimplementers.consequence: A naive JavaScript verifier reports roughly a third of an intact chain as INVALID. That is a defect in the verifier, not in the chain.
known_trap_for_reimplementers.fix: Parse the raw card bytes with a tokeniser that preserves every numeric literal exactly as sent, and re-emit that text. scripts/verify-estate.mjs does this and passes 335/335.
known_trap_for_reimplementers.why_published: Anyone reimplementing this check will hit the same wall. Publishing the trap is cheaper for them and more honest than letting them conclude our chain is broken.

what_a_pass_does_not_establish: One key signs every card. A pass proves CUSTODY, not independence — it shows CSOAI signed these bytes, not that anyone else agrees with them.
The root is signed and NOT anchored to any timechain. A pass proves WHO, and nothing here proves WHEN.
No counterparty signature exists anywhere in the estate. The chain is one-sided.
Signature validity is not measurement correctness. These checks prove the bytes are intact and authentically signed, not that a measurement is right.
doctrine: Verification is free forever. We measure; we do not certify.
